mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median 20-day return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the average 60-day return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that pushes wage inflation higher, forcing the Fed to raise rates and compressing equity multiples, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces earnings growth and increases recession risk, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of triggered periods, or the median 60-day return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between HOUST and GDPC1 where HOUST rises while GDPC1 falls signals a shift toward inventory accumulation and weak final demand, which typically precedes earnings downgrades and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND GDPC1 < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant in a multivariate regression.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in RSAFS (personal savings) indicates households are forced to spend despite higher rates, which can overheat the economy and eventually trigger a policy reversal, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases AND RSAFS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes, or the interaction term is not significant in a regression controlling for GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above trend by more than 1% for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports earnings growth and justifies higher equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > trend by >1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the effect reverses when wage growth accelerates.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises above 4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, it indicates delayed monetary policy response to inflation, which typically precedes a tightening cycle and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation expectations fall sharply.
